```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 13
    n_vehicles = 3
    Q = 115  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[84, 76], [39, 6], [80, 26], [90, 83], [61, 51], [18, 35], [26, 76], [59, 66], [67, 9], [81, 24], [48, 37], [29, 31], [35, 58]]
    demands = [22, 19, 21, 23, 19, 18, 25, 22, 5, 5, 18, 18, 16]
    time_windows = [[0, 323], [66, 147], [43, 114], [61, 148], [57, 157], [26, 113], [58, 137], [32, 102], [17, 104], [52, 108], [53, 119], [27, 89], [30, 113], [15, 80]]
    service_times = [12, 10, 6, 8, 13, 10, 5, 7, 10, 6, 6, 15, 15]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

To: Delivery Planning and Dispatch Teams
From: Logistics Operations Manager
Subject: Routing and Scheduling Framework for Today’s Deliveries

Overview
We will execute a set of deliveries from a single central depot using a fleet of identical vehicles. The plan must cover all customer stops in the service area and return vehicles to the depot within the operating day. All vehicles will depart the depot at time 0, each completing one continuous trip that visits its assigned customers in sequence and returns before depot closing.

Routing and Scheduling Challenge
- Every customer must be visited exactly once. No split deliveries or missed stops are allowed.
- Each vehicle runs a single outbound-and-return route: leave the depot at time 0, visit an ordered list of customers, and return to the depot before the depot’s closing time.
- Travel time between any two locations is the straight-line distance based on map coordinates. With an implicit speed of 1, distance units equal time units.

Time Windows and Service Rules
- Each customer has a specific delivery time window. Service must begin within this window.
- If a vehicle arrives before a customer’s window opens, it must wait on site until service can start.
- After beginning service, the vehicle remains on site for the required unloading/service time. Departure from the customer occurs at arrival time plus the service time; if waiting was required, departure occurs at window open time plus the service time.
- Arriving after a customer’s latest acceptable time is not allowed.

Capacity and Loading
- Vehicles are capacity-constrained. The total demand assigned to any vehicle must not exceed its capacity. This must hold for the route as a whole and at every point along the route.
- There are no mid-route returns to the depot for reloads and no transshipments between vehicles.

Cost Considerations
- Deploying a vehicle incurs a fixed cost per vehicle used.
- Travel distance contributes to variable cost.
- Our plan should balance the number of vehicles used and the distance traveled to achieve an overall cost-effective solution while meeting all service commitments.

Planning Goal
Build a set of vehicle routes that:
- Visit every customer exactly once.
- Respect all customer time windows and service times.
- Keep the load on each vehicle within capacity.
- Start all routes at time 0 and ensure all vehicles return to the depot before it closes.
- Minimize total travel distance plus the fixed costs associated with vehicles deployed.
